# Review — iliad-143 (Iliad 23.1–98), two passes

Edited in place by script: units.json, fields l, i, n only; t, ln, p, v and mark untouched (checked by comparison with the original after the edit). Not run: build, validate. gloss.json does not exist in the draft folder, so the second pass could not check parses against it; the glossary pass is still to do.

Severity: high = a binding house rendering or a published-English rule broken, or a meaning wrong; medium = a false or misleading note claim, a note contradicting its l or i, a scansion note owed; low = polish.

## Not fixable by the reviewer (t is not to be touched): open for the drafter or caller

1. HIGH. Unit at 62 (t ends at νήδυμος, mid-clause, no punctuation) and the next unit (t begins ἀμφιχυθείς·). The build refuses a unit whose t does not end at . ; · or a comma. The edition prints νήδυμος ἀμφιχυθείς· as one clause. Fix: move ἀμφιχυθείς· into the first unit’s t, so that unit 62 is "εὖτε τὸν ὕπνος ἔμαρπτε λύων μελεδήματα θυμοῦ\nνήδυμος ἀμφιχυθείς·" and the next begins "μάλα γὰρ κάμε φαίδιμα γυῖα" (still ln 63, still mid-line). The l, i and n of both units are already written for exactly that cut (62 l has "sweet, poured round him;", 63 l begins "for greatly had grown weary").
2. HIGH. Unit at 43 (t ends at ἱκέσθαι, line 44, no punctuation): same build refusal. Fix: merge the unit at 43 with the unit at 45 into one unit of five lines (43–47), joining l and i (l keeps its line breaks, i runs on) and merging the two notes, or cut elsewhere at a mark (κόμην, in line 46 is a comma, mid-line). The l and i of both are already sentence-continuous at this seam.
3. new-renderings.md is out of step with the edited units: the row for χαῖρέ μοι ὦ Πάτροκλε must read l "Be glad, Patroclus", i "Be glad, Patroclus", avoided "Rejoice" (the Odyssey table’s χαῖρε row), "Hail", "Farewell"; add rows for ἠθείη κεφαλή (follows the table’s ἠθεῖος "honoured"), γέρας (unchanged), ἀμφιφορεύς (Odyssey table, "amphora"/"jar"); the row for ἀκάματον πῦρ gives i "the untiring fire" against the table’s "an untiring fire" (left, see refused). The λοετρά "washing-water" (23.44) has no row: it departs from 22.443 "warm baths" and the table turns "bath-water" down; the drafter should list it with a reason, or choose "baths".
4. gloss.json is absent; the glosser’s parses were not checked (second pass could not read it).
5. The packet lists 23.23 as a repeat of a line in iliad-119, but the Greek there is ἀποδειροτομήσω and here ἀποδειροτομήσειν, so nothing is enforced; the English here (infinitive, still under ὑπέστην) is rightly different.

## Checks that came out clean

Speech marks: five speeches (6–11, 19–23, 43–53, 69–92, 94–98), each “ on its first unit with mark, ” on its last, 5 and 5 in both layers. No speech runs on from iliad-142 (its last unit, 515, is narration) and none runs into 23.99 (ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας is narration; the root has no iliad-144 file yet, the source line was read). Repeated lines: 23.3, 23.54, 23.93 identical to the published units; 23.17–18 now identical to iliad-119; 23.24, 23.33, 23.56, 23.57 take the published wording; 23.62 and 23.68 take the Odyssey’s. Cross-references in notes (iliad-125, 141, 056, 052, 005, 119, 001; odyssey-098, odyssey-021) checked against the packet. Positional claims (mid-line beginnings at 14, 26, 29, 63, 95; ἠῶθεν in the next line; λαοί at 53; δώσειν in the last unit) checked. p flags at 1, 12, 24, 35, 54, 93 agree with the edition’s paragraphs.

## Findings considered and refused

- 4 i "drive close": ἰόντες is "going", but the horses are yoked and ridden, so "drive" is the sense in the English layer; l keeps "going".
- 6–7 note: ‘prohibition in the subjunctive’ for μὴ δή πω λυώμεθα: it is a negative exhortation, and the note says ‘let us not yet loose’; label left.
- 63 l "had grown weary" for an aorist after γάρ: the English pluperfect is the idiom the part uses elsewhere (ἐπεὶ … ἵκοντο "had come"); left.
- 69 i "and have forgotten me" for αὐτάρ: force is slightly weaker than "but" but the English reads naturally; l has "but".
- 59 l/i "much-roaring" / "loud-roaring": the table’s own l/i split; the note quotes the i form, which is true of i.
- 52 "the untiring fire" against the table’s "an untiring fire": the fire is the particular pyre-fire, so the article is the English sentence’s; left, and listed above for the drafter to record.
- 19 and 84 δόμοισι "houses" / "house": both appear in the published parts for the same plural dative (138.52 "houses of Hades", odyssey-100 "house of Hades"); left.
- 53 ἔργα "tasks": no table row; plain sense of "works" in context; left.
- 54 κλύον "imperfect": the published note for the same line (iliad-052) takes the same label; left.
- 25 ὅς τίς τε "in a general statement": harmless; left.
- 77–79 i "never again" for οὐ: interpretive but the sense of the sentence; left.
- ὄτρυνον "imperative": true (aorist imperative), not changed.
- Line 2 ἵκοντο: not treated as an irregularity; the only licence is ἐπεί (noted).
